A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PEO in the presence of PVP and filler, yields a bioadhesive, swellable, non disintegrating, gastroretentive dosage form which is capable of retaining its integrity in the stomach for about 9 h.
the polyethylene oxide (polyox WSR N-80) in combination with Povidone (Kollidon 30) yields a non disintigrating type of bioadhesive dosage forms which are suitable for gastroretention applications.
PVP/PEO based bioadhesive polyethylene oxide (PVOH) compacts are suitable for gastric retention and can be used as gastroretentive drug delivery systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PVP-PEO based bioadhesive dosage forms can be used for the controlled release of water insoluble compounds from the stomach.
the PEO/PVP combination can be used to formulate bioadhesive, gastroretentive, sustained-release, oral drug delivery systems for both water soluble and water-insoluble drugs.
polyethylene oxide (PVP) is a promising bioadhesive material for developing gastroretentive drug delivery systems.
